answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the release went out and is now 5x target — the temporal correlation makes the release the leading hypothesis. Memory b1 records that a rollback cleared a prior customer-facing degradation without impact, which supports rollback as the most causal single intervention. Failover (b2) fits a regional-degradation pattern, but if the new build is the cause, shifting regions may carry the defect with it and failing over the write path at settlement peak risks in-flight writes. Read replicas (b5) address read/report load, not write latency, and a circuit breaker (b4) targets a partner dependency outage with no evidence here. Key risk flagged: rolling back during peak settlement writes could disrupt in-flight transactions, so the rollback should be executed with write-drain/ordering safeguards; residual uncertainty remains that the latency is load-driven from the settlement peak rather than the release, in which case capacity (b3) would have been the better lever.
